name: Ravyn Lenae
label: Atlantic
lede: She paid $300 for her first studio session as a high school sophomore, signed to Atlantic at 16, and then made everyone wait until she was 23 for the album.

eras.title: A free download and a record deal
eras.text: A Chicago High School for the Arts student walks into Classick Studios, meets Monte Booker and Smino, and puts out a free EP. Atlantic signs her at 16.

years.h: She pays $300 for a studio session and gets "Greetings"
years.p: Ravyn Lenae is a sophomore at the Chicago High School for the Arts, where she studies classical music, when she books the time.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, she spent $300 on a studio session as a high school sophomore to produce "Greetings". She had started writing songs back at Roseland Christian School on Chicago's South Side, and her maternal grandfather, Richard Williams, was a doo-wop group member and longtime pastor there.

years.h: Moon Shoes goes up as a free download
years.p: Her debut EP comes out in August 2015, made around Chris "Classick" Innumerable's Chicago studio with [[Monte Booker|3a8d955f-fe39-4092-97e7-29f9ada69490]] and [[Smino|96800e05-9924-4321-859a-76e0d4750f2f]].
years.xp:
Classick Studios is where she met Smino in 2015, and it is where the Zero Fatigue collective formed, with Booker, Lenae and Smino at its core, per Wikipedia. She had already been featured on Booker's "Baby" that year.

Atlantic later reissued Moon Shoes (2016) through Three Twenty Three Music Group.

eras.title: Two tours and a producer who gets her
eras.text: Noname and SZA take her on the road, Steve Lacy of The Internet produces a whole EP, and R&B people in the know start saying her name.

years.h: Sixteen, signed to Atlantic, and still in high school
years.p: Atlantic reissues Moon Shoes through Three Twenty Three Music Group. She also turns up on Mick Jenkins' The Healing Component and on [[Noname|1395c84b-2e84-4f25-9962-f1c0d5aa31ed]]'s "Forever".
years.xp: W Magazine reports she signed with Atlantic at 16 and toured with Noname while still in high school. Wikipedia dates the signing and the Atlantic and Three Twenty Three reissue of Moon Shoes to 2016.

years.h: Noname's first tour, then SZA's Ctrl run
years.p: Noname's Telefone tour runs January to March 2017, and [[SZA|272989c8-5535-492d-a25c-9f58803e027f]]'s Ctrl tour picks her up from August to December.
years.xp:
Refinery29 says Noname took her on her first tour and that the SZA run, the same year, convinced her she could headline on her own. She graduated high school in May 2017.

Of the two runs she said: "Being able to be on those tours so young, with Black women was really special for me."

years.h: Rolling Stone and SXSW find Midnight Moonlight
years.p: Rolling Stone puts her on its "10 New Artists You Need to Know" list that March, and she plays SXSW.
years.xp: Rolling Stone said the EP "delves into more romantic concerns with the same quiet grace", as quoted on Wikipedia.

years.h: Steve Lacy produces all five songs on Crush
years.p: Lacy executive-produces the EP and writes every track with her; he sings on "Computer Luv" and "4 Leaf Clover".
years.xp: Wikipedia lists five tracks and a 16:33 running time. Pitchfork called it suited to "Quiet Storm radio" with a "methodical late-night vibe". Gothamist put it on its 2018 year-end albums list, and she performed on MTV's Total Request Live.

eras.title: The album takes its time
eras.text: She starts in 2019, loses the plan to the pandemic, moves from Chicago to Los Angeles, and finishes a 16-track debut that Pitchfork ranks No. 32 of 2022.

years.h: She starts Hypnos and commutes between Chicago and LA
years.p: She begins the album after touring Crush, meeting producers in both cities. Ravyn Lenae said it in W Magazine, on why the wait ran so long.
years.xp:
The pandemic interrupted the process in 2020, and she moved from Chicago to Los Angeles that August. She finished mastering three days before W Magazine's May 2022 interview.

The full line: "I can make songs all day. It's not about making enough songs. It's about making songs that feel like now." Of the four-year gap she added: "I just want people to really understand why it took me this long. It's a project of growth."

years.h: "Skin Tight" brings Steve Lacy back for the first single
years.p: It opens a run of four singles, followed by "Light Me Up", "M.I.A." and the [[Kaytranada|e56aee57-d90e-40cf-a70d-beb70f6f3c69]]-produced "Xtasy".

years.h: Pitchfork gives Hypnos an 8.5 and Best New Music
years.p: The review calls the debut "a mature reintroduction"; NPR Music ranks it No. 18 of 2022 and Pitchfork lands it at No. 32.
years.xp:
Produced by Luke Titus, Steve Lacy, Monte Booker, Kaytranada, Sango and IAmNobodi, per Wikipedia, with recording running 2018 to 2022. Clash and Loud and Quiet each gave it 8/10. Complex placed it No. 30 and The A.V. Club No. 22 on year-end lists.

An "Xtasy" remix with Doechii followed in September 2022.

years.h: She brings a six-piece band to the NPR building
years.p: Her Tiny Desk is one of the first concerts back in the office, with Harrison "Achee" Hawkins on keys. The set: "Venom", "Skin Tight", "Inside Out", "Sticky".
years.xp: NPR's page lists bassist Marcus Reddick, drummer Danielle "Dee" Thompson, guitarist Garrett Jones and backing vocalists Aja Grant and Phylilia Hill. On "Inside Out" she said self-love is "a lifelong journey".

eras.title: The slow song that took over
eras.text: A second album with DJ Dahi, a TikTok mashup with Solange that shows up six months late, and a Hot 100 top five.

years.h: Bird's Eye arrives with DJ Dahi running the room
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 7.8; Metacritic lists 83 from six reviews. Ty Dolla $ign and [[Childish Gambino|7fb57fba-a6ef-44c2-abab-2fa3bdee607e]] guest.
years.xp: It was recorded in 2023 across three North Hollywood and Burbank studios, with Dahi and 11 other producers including Steve Lacy, Terry Lewis and Rascal. The lead singles "Love Is Blind" and "Love Me Not" came out on May 3, 2024. She described the record as "a return to a place of self-trust".

years.cap: Ravyn Lenae at Way Out West festival, August 2026
years.src: Wikipedia: Love Me Not · Wikipedia: Ravyn Lenae
years.h: A TikTok mashup with Solange drags "Love Me Not" to No. 5
years.p: A user posts it over Solange's "Losing You" six months after release; the song climbs to No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the mashup came from a TikTok user called thatsode, and the song was soundtracking over 320,000 clips by April 2025. It entered the Hot 100 at No. 81 and climbed to No. 5, and reached No. 2 in the UK and Australia.

Certifications cited include 2x Platinum in the UK and 5x Platinum in Canada.

years.h: She opens for Sabrina Carpenter, plays Coachella, then headlines
years.p: [[Sabrina Carpenter|1882fe91-cdd9-49c9-9956-8e06a3810bd4]]'s Short n' Sweet Tour comes first, Coachella in April, then her own shows in the US, UK and Europe that fall.
years.xp: Billboard named her R&B Rookie of the Year among its R&B/Hip-Hop Power Players, and "Love Me Not" was nominated for Song of Summer at the MTV VMAs, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Ravyn Lenae at the WWD Style Awards, January 2026
years.p: Her next album, Blue Island, was scheduled for August 7, 2026.
